items.stem: Arjun writes (2 × 10⁷) + (2 × 10⁷) = 4 × 10¹⁴. Explain the error and give the correct answer in standard form.
items.markingKey: When adding, the powers of 10 are not added; factor out 10⁷ (R1 M1); 4 × 10⁷ (A1).

items.stem: Mei writes: "6 × 10⁻⁴ is a negative number." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: A negative exponent gives a small positive number: 6 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.0006.
items.markingKey: A negative exponent gives a small positive number: 6 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.0006. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A red blood cell has a diameter of about 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ m. Find how many such cells would fit in a line of length 9.0 × 10⁻² m. Give your answer in the form a × 10ᵏ, where 1 ≤ a < 10, k ∈ ℤ, to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: Correct operation set up (M1); evaluate (A1); 1.20 × 10⁴ cells (A1).

items.stem:
Scientific notation is used to describe a journey to Jupiter.
(a) The radius of Jupiter is 6.99 × 10⁷ m. Find its volume, assuming it is a sphere.
(b) A spacecraft travels 6.29 × 10¹¹ m to Jupiter at an average speed of 1.5 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. Find the time taken in seconds.
(c) Convert this time to days, to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: (a) V = (4/3)πr³ (M1) A1 (b) time = distance ÷ speed (M1) A1 (c) ÷ 86 400 (M1) A1 [Total 6 marks]

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "order of magnitude"?
options: The sum of the terms of an arithmetic sequence: Sₙ = (n/2)(2u₁ + (n − 1)d) = (n/2)(u₁ + uₙ)
The power of 10 in the standard form of a number, used to compare sizes
A series whose partial sums Sₙ approach a finite limit as n → ∞
The sum of terms of a geometric sequence: Sₙ = u₁(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1), r ≠ 1
items.answer: The power of 10 in the standard form of a number, used to compare sizes
items.markingKey: B. "order of magnitude" is the power of 10 in the standard form of a number, used to compare sizes.

items.stem: Explain how to add 3.2 × 10⁵ and 4.1 × 10⁴ in standard form.
items.answer: Rewrite with the same power of ten: 3.2 × 10⁵ + 0.41 × 10⁵ = 3.61 × 10⁵; exponents are not simply added.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Rewrite with the same power of ten: 3.2 × 10⁵ + 0.41 × 10⁵ = 3.61 × 10⁵; exponents are not simply added. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Without a calculator, find (5 × 10⁴) × (6 × 10²), giving your answer in the form a × 10ᵏ where 1 ≤ a < 10, k ∈ ℤ.
items.markingKey: multiply/divide the numbers and add/subtract the indices (M1); adjust so that 1 ≤ a < 10 (M1); 3 × 10⁷ (A1).

items.stem: "(2 × 10³) + (3 × 10³) = 5 × 10⁶." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Only the numbers are added when the powers are equal: 5 × 10³.
items.markingKey: Only the numbers are added when the powers are equal: 5 × 10³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:

(b) A spacecraft travels 4.14 × 10¹⁰ m to Venus at an average speed of 1.1 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. Find the time taken in seconds.
(c) Convert this time to days, to 3 significant figures.

items.stem: Explain whether the sequence 4, 9, 13, 19, 24, … could be arithmetic.
items.answer: not arithmetic: differences are not constant
items.markingKey: Differences are 5, 4, 6, 5 (M1); not all equal, so no common difference (R1); not arithmetic (A1).

items.stem: The sum of the first n terms of the series 3 + 5 + 7 + … is 624. Find n.
items.markingKey: (n/2)(2(3) + (n − 1)(2)) = 624 (M1); 2n² + 4n − 1248 = 0 (A1); solve, reject the negative root (M1 R1); n = 24 (A1).

(a) Given that u₃ = −3 and u₇ = 21, find the first term and the common difference.
(b) Find the sum of the first 17 terms.
(c) Find the first term of the sequence that is positive.

items.stem:
This question investigates arithmetic series and their sums.
(a) Prove that the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series is Sₙ = (n/2)(2u₁ + (n − 1)d).
(b) A sequence is defined by uᵣ = 2r + 7. Show that it is arithmetic.
(c) Find an expression for Σ from r = 1 to n of uᵣ in its simplest form.
(d) Hence find Σ from r = 51 to 100 of uᵣ.
(e) Prove that if a, b, c are consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence then b = (a + c)/2.
items.markingKey: (a) write Sₙ forwards and backwards (M1); add (M1); 2Sₙ = n(2u₁ + (n − 1)d) (A1) AG (b) uᵣ₊₁ − uᵣ = 2, a constant (M1 R1) (c) M1 A1 (d) S₁₀₀ − S₅₀ (M1) A1 (e) b − a = c − b (M1); rearrange (A1) [Total 11 marks]

items.stem: The 30th term of the arithmetic sequence 11, 15, 19, 23, … is
Which of the following best describes "arithmetic sequence"?
options: A sequence with a constant difference d between consecutive terms: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d
Writing a number as a × 10ᵏ with 1 ≤ a < 10 and k an integer
The power of 10 in the standard form of a number, used to compare sizes
The constant amount d = uₙ₊₁ − uₙ added to each term of an arithmetic sequence to get the next
items.answer: A sequence with a constant difference d between consecutive terms: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d
items.markingKey: A. "arithmetic sequence" is a sequence with a constant difference d between consecutive terms: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d.

items.stem: Explain why the formula Sₙ = (n/2)(u₁ + uₙ) works for an arithmetic series.
items.answer: Writing the series forwards and backwards and adding pairs each term with its mirror term; every pair sums to u₁ + uₙ, there are n pairs, so 2Sₙ = n(u₁ + uₙ).
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Writing the series forwards and backwards and adding pairs each term with its mirror term; every pair sums to u₁ + uₙ, there are n pairs, so 2Sₙ = n(u₁ + uₙ). (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the sequence 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, … appears to be arithmetic and write down a formula for its nth term.
items.markingKey: Each difference is 5 (R1); u₁ = 2 (A1); uₙ = 2 + (n − 1)5 = 5n − 3 (A1).

items.stem: Explain how to show that three numbers form consecutive terms of a geometric sequence.
items.answer: Show the ratio of the second to the first equals the ratio of the third to the second (equivalently b² = ac).

items.stem: Explain why logarithms are needed to find the number of terms of a geometric sequence that are less than a given value.

items.stem: The numbers p, p + 2 and p + 10 are consecutive terms of a geometric sequence. Explain why (p + 2)² = p(p + 10), and hence find p.

items.markingKey: Ratios equal: (p + 5)/p = (p + 20)/(p + 5) (R1); cross-multiply (M1); p = 5/2 (A1).
